title: Urban Bear NYC Street Fair
description: The 18th annual Urban Bear street fair takes over Little West 12th Street with music, vendors, community groups, and a large outdoor bear-community gathering.
venue: Little West 12th Street between Washington Street and 10th Avenue
fit_reason: A major gay community event in Manhattan with an easygoing outdoor format.

title: Broadway Flea Market & Grand Auction
description: Broadway Cares celebrates the event’s 40th year with more than 60 tables of theatrical collectibles, an autograph and photo area, and live and silent auctions.
venue: Shubert Alley, West 44th and West 45th Streets, and Times Square
price_label: Free to browse; auction and merchandise prices vary
fit_reason: A Broadway-lover’s treasure hunt near Hell’s Kitchen, with memorabilia and performers.

title: 2026 Magical Girls Festival
description: An all-ages convention devoted to magical-girl anime and manga, with screenings, vendors, activities, panels, cosplay, voice actors, and a Madoka Magica anniversary spotlight.
venue: 5-2-A at Industry City, 33 35th Street, 2nd Floor
fit_reason: A focused anime-and-manga day with screenings and fan programming at a modest price.

title: Give Us Our Daily Dread: Horror Comics
description: James Tynion IV, Chris Condon, and Ezra Claytan Daniels discuss the continuing growth of horror comics and their recent graphic novels at the Brooklyn Book Festival.
venue: Borough Hall Courtroom, 209 Joralemon Street
fit_reason: A free panel squarely about comics, graphic novels, and genre storytelling.

title: Fall Into Fantasy
description: Fantasy authors Sarah Beth Durst, Amélie Wen Zhao, and Shannon J. Spann discuss worldbuilding, magic, romance, power, and family in their recent novels.
venue: Brooklyn Law School Student Lounge, 250 Joralemon Street
fit_reason: A free fiction event devoted to imaginative worlds and the craft behind them.

title: Call of Games presented by NYU
description: Novelists and nonfiction writers discuss how video games and novels influence one another and expand storytelling across both media in this virtual Brooklyn Book Festival program.
venue: Online via Zoom
fit_reason: It directly combines video games and fiction, and it is free to join from home.

title: Game-A-Palooza 2026
description: IGDA NYC’s curated indie-game showcase opens its locally made and unreleased games to the public, with opportunities to play and meet New York developers.
venue: 339 Adams Street
fit_reason: Hands-on access to unreleased games and local developers for only $10.

title: New York Comic Con 2026
description: NYCC’s 20th-anniversary edition spans comics, anime, manga, science fiction, gaming, authors, cosplay, film, television, exhibitors, and creator appearances.
venue: Jacob K. Javits Convention Center, 429 11th Avenue
price_label: Adult single-day tickets $103.98–$114.86 including taxes and fees; availability varies
fit_reason: A nearby convention bringing comics, manga, anime, science fiction, and gaming together.

title: Extreme Codesign for Efficient AI: Algorithms, Software, and Hardware
description: Cornell Tech professor Mohamed Abdelfattah presents techniques for reducing AI inference bottlenecks across numerical representation, tensor compression, software, and accelerator hardware.
venue: NYU Tandon School of Engineering, 370 Jay Street, Room 825
fit_reason: A technical deep dive at the hardware-software boundary of modern AI systems.

title: Maker Faire Coney Island 2026
description: A three-day interactive festival of inventions and DIY projects with exhibits, demonstrations, workshops, competitions, robotics, engineering, crafts, and 3D printing.
venue: Coney Island Amphitheater
fit_reason: The strongest hands-on match for maker, electronics, robotics, and prototyping interests.

title: Climate Resilience in the Age of AI
description: A Climate Week NYC panel examines FloodNet sensors, the ClimateIQ risk platform, next-generation flood maps, and privacy, equity, and energy questions around climate technology.
venue: NYU Tandon MakerSpace, 6 MetroTech Center, Room 116
fit_reason: It combines AI, NYC infrastructure, sensors, and a MakerSpace setting.

title: From Risk Maps to Resilience Investments: Making Climate AI Decision-Ready
description: Researchers and leaders from city government, infrastructure planning, finance, and insurance examine how climate-risk models can guide resilience investment through a demo, workshop, panel, and networking.
venue: NYU Tandon CUSP Learning Commons, 370 Jay Street, Floor 13
fit_reason: A direct connection between quantitative modeling, finance, insurance, and NYC infrastructure decisions.

title: Zumba in the Park
description: A free, high-energy full-body workout combining aerobic exercise with Latin-inspired dance moves. All fitness levels are welcome.
venue: Fort Tryon Park volleyball courts by the 190th Street station elevators
fit_reason: A free and approachable outdoor class for easing back into a fitness routine.

title: Dance Fitness at West Harlem Piers
description: A free Shape Up NYC dance-fitness class in West Harlem with rotating instructors and programming suitable for all fitness levels.
venue: West Harlem Piers Park, 125th Street and Marginal Street
fit_reason: A nearby, social, no-cost way to restart a fitness routine without a gym commitment.

title: Jazz in the Park at Ralph Ellison
description: Berta Indeed presents Let the Music Play, a free community concert featuring local jazz musicians and vocalists at Ralph Ellison Plaza.
venue: Ralph Ellison Plaza, Riverside Drive and West 150th Street
fit_reason: Free community jazz uptown, close enough to feel genuinely easy rather than aspirationally nearby.

title: Harvest Festival at Randall’s Island
description: A free outdoor fall festival with a pumpkin patch, seasonal cooking demonstrations, live performances, face painting, and hands-on nature activities.
venue: Urban Farm and Fields 62/63, Randall's Island Park
fit_reason: A free fall afternoon combining food programming, light activity, nature, and community entertainment.

title: The 51st Annual Atlantic Antic
description: A mile-long neighborhood street festival with hundreds of vendors, food, crafts, shopping, live music, entertainment, and family areas along Atlantic Avenue.
venue: Atlantic Avenue from Hicks Street to Fourth Avenue
price_label: Free admission; food and merchandise vary
fit_reason: A big food-and-culture street festival with live music and plenty to browse.

title: Piano in Bryant Park
description: A free outdoor piano program featuring ragtime, stride, and jazz on Bryant Park’s Upper Terrace during lunchtime.
venue: Upper Terrace, Bryant Park
fit_reason: A casual, free daytime jazz option that does not require a full evening commitment.

title: Art History Happy Hour: Sculpting the Senses
description: A lighthearted evening of short talks by experts in art, mathematics, and material science, followed by after-hours access to Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses.
venue: Brooklyn Museum, 200 Eastern Parkway
price_label: $30; $18 for members; includes exhibition access and one specialty drink
fit_reason: A museum social combining art, fashion, mathematics, material science, and after-hours exhibition access.

title: Día de los Muertos at NYBG
description: A monthlong celebration of memory, life, and renewal featuring marigold displays, a community ofrenda, calaveras, a flower-covered Catrina, weekend music and crafts, and special performances.
venue: New York Botanical Garden, 2900 Southern Boulevard
fit_reason: A substantial cultural celebration in the Bronx with botanical displays, art, music, crafts, and community traditions.
